transcription.tex: Why is a door handle usually far from the hinge?
For a given force, increasing its perpendicular distance from the hinge increases the turning effect.
If the perpendicular distance is doubled, what happens to the force required to produce the same turning effect?
The required force halves. The product of force and perpendicular distance stays the same.

transcription.tex: \textbf{From particles to rigid bodies}\par A particle model ignores an object’s dimensions. A rigid-body model includes its size and shape, so it can describe rotation.\par A rod is a thin rigid body. A lamina is a thin, flat body.

\textbf{Three ideas in this chapter}\par 1. Equilibrium: the resultant force and resultant moment are both zero.\par 2. Centre of mass: a uniform rod’s weight acts at its midpoint; a non-uniform rod’s need not.\par 3. Tilting: a support about to lose contact exerts no reaction. Use the remaining pivot to take moments.

transcription.tex: \textbf{Moment of a force about a point}\[M=Fd\] Here \(d\) is the \textbf{perpendicular distance} from the point to the force’s line of action. Units: newton metres, \(\mathrm{N\,m}\).
A light seesaw carries a 700 N weight on the left and a 75 kg mass on the right. Which way does it turn about \(A\)?
Anticlockwise: \(700(10)=7000\,\mathrm{N\,m}\).\par Clockwise: \(75g(8)=5880\,\mathrm{N\,m}\).
The anticlockwise moment is greater: resultant \(1120\,\mathrm{N\,m}\) anticlockwise.

transcription.tex: Find each moment about \(P\), including its direction.\par 1. A 20 N force acts downwards 10 m to the right of \(P\).\par 2. A 20 N force has a line of action through \(P\).\par 3. A 10 N force acts at \(60^\circ\) below a horizontal rod, 5 m to the right of \(P\).
1. \(20(10)=200\,\mathrm{N\,m}\) clockwise.\par 2. Zero: perpendicular distance is zero.\par 3. \(10(5\sin60^\circ)=43.3\,\mathrm{N\,m}\) clockwise.
4. A 10 N force acts at \(30^\circ\) above a horizontal rod, 2 m to the right of \(P\).\par 5. A 5 N force acts \(65^\circ\) from the upward vertical, 3 m to the right of \(P\).
4. \(10(2\sin30^\circ)=10\,\mathrm{N\,m}\) anticlockwise.\par 5. \(5(3\cos65^\circ)=6.34\,\mathrm{N\,m}\) anticlockwise.
For a right triangle with hypotenuse \(r\): opposite side \(r\sin\theta\), adjacent side \(r\cos\theta\).

transcription.tex: \textbf{Resultant moments}\par Choose clockwise or anticlockwise as positive and add signed moments. Find these resultants about \(P\).\par 1. 20 N downwards, 10 m right; 10 N downwards, 15 m left.\par 2. 5 N downwards, 3 m right; 4 N upwards, 1 m right; 3 N downwards, 1 m left.
1. \(200-150=50\,\mathrm{N\,m}\) clockwise.\par 2. \(15-4-3=8\,\mathrm{N\,m}\) clockwise.

3. A light rod carries 50 kg at 1 m left of \(P\), and 30 kg at 3 m right of \(P\).\par 4. A light rod has length \(x\) m. Pivot \(P\) is 4 m from its left end; a 30 kg mass hangs at its right end \((x>4)\).

transcription.tex: A light horizontal rod has pivot \(P\). A 6 N downward force acts 3 m left of \(P\); a 4 N force acts 3 m right, at \(40^\circ\) above the rod; a 5 N force acts 4 m right, at \(80^\circ\) below the rod. Find the resultant moment.
Perpendicular distances are \(3\), \(3\sin40^\circ\), and \(4\sin80^\circ\) metres.

transcription.tex: 1. A rectangular barge is 120 m long and 20 m wide. It is fixed at its bottom-right corner \(P\). At the top-left, a 2000 N force acts down-left at \(45^\circ\) to the vertical; at the bottom-left, 1100 N acts down-right at \(60^\circ\) below the horizontal. Find the resultant moment and state a modelling assumption.

Anticlockwise moment:\[2000(120\cos45^\circ+20\sin45^\circ)\] \[+1100(120\sin60^\circ)=332309\,\mathrm{N\,m}.\] \(332\,\mathrm{kN\,m}\) anticlockwise. Model the barge as a rigid lamina, with no other turning forces.

2. A uniform aircraft door \(AB\), length 4 m and weight 2500 N, is hinged at \(B\). It is inclined at \(45^\circ\) to the horizontal. A vertical upward force at \(A\) tends to lift the door. Find the force needed to start lifting.
At the threshold:\[F(4\cos45^\circ)=2500(2\cos45^\circ).\]\[F=1250\text{ N}.\] A force greater than this starts lifting.

transcription.tex: \textbf{Equilibrium of a rigid body}\par Both conditions are required:\[\sum\mathbf F=\mathbf0,\qquad\sum M=0.\]\par For vertical forces, total upward force equals total downward force. About any point, total clockwise moment equals total anticlockwise moment.

\textbf{A reliable method}\par 1. Draw the external forces.\par 2. Place a uniform rod’s weight at its midpoint.\par 3. Resolve forces.\par 4. Take moments about a point that eliminates an unwanted force.\par 5. Check units and the physical meaning of the answer.

transcription.tex: A uniform seesaw has length 18 m and mass 20 kg. Its pivot \(P\) is 10 m from the left end. Woody (70 kg) sits at the left end; Buzz (\(m\) kg) sits at the right. Find \(m\) and the pivot reaction \(R\).
Moments about \(P\):\[70g(10)+20g(1)=mg(8).\]\[m=90\text{ kg}.\] Vertical forces give \(R=180g=1764\) N.
Alternatively, moments about \(B\):\[8R=70g(18)+20g(9).\] Hence \(R=1764\) N, then \(R=(70+20+m)g\) gives \(m=90\) kg.

a) Horizontal equilibrium gives \(R_A=60\) N.\par b) Moments about \(B\):\[60(8\sin70^\circ)=mg(4\cos70^\circ).\]\[m=\frac{120\tan70^\circ}{g}=33.6\text{ kg (3 s.f.)}.\]

transcription.tex: 6. A non-uniform beam \(PQ\), length \(8a\) and mass \(m\), hangs from wires at \(M,N\), with \(PM=a\), \(QN=2a\). A particle of mass \(\tfrac34m\) at \(Q\) brings it to the point of tipping about \(N\).\par a) Show that \(ON=\tfrac32a\), where \(O\) is the centre of mass.\par b) Move the particle to the midpoint. Find the tension at \(N\).
At tipping, \(T_M=0\). Moments about \(N\):\[mg(ON)=\tfrac34mg(2a).\]\[ON=\tfrac32a.\]
\(PO=6a-1.5a=4.5a\). Moments about \(M\) after moving the particle:\[T_N(5a)=mg(3.5a)+\tfrac34mg(3a).\]\[T_N=\frac{23}{20}mg.\]

transcription.tex: 7. A uniform beam \(AB\) has length 14 m and weight \(W\). It hangs from vertical cables at \(C,D\), with \(AC=4\) m and \(BD=6\) m. A 180 N weight at \(A\) brings it to the point of tilting. Replace it with a weight \(V\) at \(B\). Find the maximum \(V\) for equilibrium.
First, \(T_D=0\). Moments about \(C\):\[180(4)=3W\quad\Rightarrow\quad W=240\text{ N}.\] At maximum \(V\), \(T_C=0\). About \(D\):\[240(1)=6V\quad\Rightarrow\quad V=40\text{ N}.\]
